answer: Crystal Ledger Decay. Each identity carries a decaying balance that only refills through verified reciprocal trades; new identities start at a nectar-thin baseline. Cloning forces the attacker to subsidize real activity per clone, so cost scales linearly with fleet size rather than paying once. An opal-tier audit threshold triggers on clusters of young, low-history identities, freezing their balances until genuine trade resumes. Attacker cost: sustained subsidy of every clone's baseline, plus forgone audit fees.
